$comment: Per-repo config for THIS repo's own ratcheted PR/push source-leak run (self-source-leak-gate.yml passes it via the reusable gate's `config` input; consuming repos never receive it). ONE exemption class, the same self-referential false positive config/self-check.json documents at length: files that must carry a gate's OWN literal name, which the SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule reads as a planning-artifact marker. skills-drift-gate.yml is the gate's own reusable workflow — its steps invoke scripts out of the gate checkout directory named after the gate, an irreducible reference (all rephraseable prose mentions on changed lines are reworded instead, per the rephrase-first doctrine). self-check.json is the hermetic self-check's exemption ledger — its entries LIST such gate filenames verbatim, so any edit to the ledger line would otherwise trip the ratchet that this config exists to calibrate. This file itself is self-exempt (the engine exempts the --config path). The parity fixture corpus is skipped by prefix and lines marked source-leak-allow are exempt: planted detector test input and the engine's own rationale comments must be able to carry the phrasings the gate bans. Engine+test pair exemption: source-leak-gate.test.mjs and source-leak-ratchet.test.mjs carry the private names AS deliberate test inputs, scattered through the whole file (the same class as the other engine+test pairs the org exempts). The ENGINE is deliberately NOT exempted here, and never will be. It needs no whole-file exemption and is actively harmed by one: the engine already protects exactly the region that must carry the markers — the sentinel-bracketed rule definitions — and scans the rest of itself normally, so a whole-file exemption would discard a real leak anywhere outside that region. A marker-bearing line the engine must carry OUTSIDE the rule-definition region is exempted at the LINE with source-leak-allow, never by re-adding the file. The FIXTURE's basename entry is a different animal: it is TIME-BOXED, not permanent. The current engine skips the fixture by real path, but this repository's own caller runs a PINNED engine out of a separate checkout, and there the real-path skip resolves to that checkout's own copy of the fixture — so the fixture in the scanned tree is read by that engine and every marker line planted in it counts as a finding. The basename entry covers exactly that gap, and exemptFileBasenamesExpiry keys it to the pin that creates the gap — to the exact `uses:` target the caller invokes, not merely to some sha somewhere in that file, so moving THAT reference off the pinned commit expires the entry even while unrelated action pins stay put: while the caller still pins that commit the entry is live and the gate says nothing about it; the moment the pin moves the gate fails and the basename and its expiry entry are deleted together, in the same change.
